hook: This is the greatest achievement in basketball you never knew existed.
story: March 2nd, 1962. A half-empty arena in Hershey, Pennsylvania. No TV cameras. No New York reporters. That night, Wilt Chamberlain scored 100 points in one NBA game. The Knicks spent the final quarter holding the ball and fouling his teammates - a whole team playing keep-away from one man. It didn't work. When he hit 100, two hundred fans stormed the court. And here is the strange part: no film of that game has ever been found. Nobody alive has watched it.
number: In 64 years, nobody has come within 17 points of his record. That same season, he averaged 50.4 points a game.
closer: All that survives is a box score, a radio tape - and one photograph, taken by a photographer who wasn't even working that night.
full_text: This is the greatest achievement in basketball you never knew existed. March 2nd, 1962. A half-empty arena in Hershey, Pennsylvania. No TV cameras. No New York reporters. That night, Wilt Chamberlain scored 100 points in one NBA game. The Knicks spent the final quarter holding the ball and fouling his teammates - a whole team playing keep-away from one man. It didn't work. When he hit 100, two hundred fans stormed the court. And here is the strange part: no film of that game has ever been found. Nobody alive has watched it. In 64 years, nobody has come within 17 points of his record. That same season, he averaged 50.4 points a game. All that survives is a box score, a radio tape - and one photograph, taken by a photographer who wasn't even working that night.
